Losing our first big customer was the best thing that ever happened to Ledgerline. Let me explain. 5 months in, they walked away. It stung. A lot. But here's the thing — failure isn't the opposite of success. It's part of it. The reason? They had heavily customized their NetSuite instance, and we only supported standard fields. We weren't meeting them where they were. So we did what great teams do: we listened. We learned. We built. We spent 6 weeks adding support for custom fields. Not just a feature — a fundamental shift in how we think about our customers. Today, we serve 38 customers. 11 of them rely on custom fields. The lesson? Your biggest setback can become your biggest breakthrough. Lean into the hard feedback. Your customers are telling you what to build — you just have to listen. What's a loss that shaped your company? #Startups #SaaS #Leadership #CustomerSuccess #Growth

1,200 repositories. 🤯 When we launched Patchwork CI, we made a promise: always free for open source. Many people told us we were crazy. "How will you make money?" they asked. Fast forward to today — we're running on 1,200 repositories, and about 900 of them are open source. 💚 But here's what truly blew my mind 👇 Across all those repos, 1 in 7 CI failures turned out to be a flaky test. Let that sink in. 1 in 7. That's countless hours of developer time wasted on red builds that weren't real failures. Open source didn't just give us users. It gave us data, feedback, and a community. In fact, our most-requested feature — GitLab support — came straight from OSS maintainers, and we shipped it on November 12. 🚀 Giving back isn't charity. It's strategy. #OpenSource #DevOps #CI #DeveloperExperience #BuildInPublic

We built a beautiful app. Nobody used it. 📱❌ When we launched Rotaship, we were so proud of our sleek, modern mobile app. We thought restaurant staff would love it. Reality check: only 12% of staff even opened it in the first month. 😳 That's when it hit us. We weren't solving the real problem. We were adding another one. Restaurant teams don't want another app. They live on WhatsApp. So in 2025, we made a tough call — we moved everything into WhatsApp. 💬 The results speak for themselves: ✅ 140 outlets ✅ Median reply time to shift messages: under 20 minutes The lesson? Meet your users where they already are. Don't make them come to you. Sometimes the best product decision is letting go of the thing you love. 💡 #ProductManagement #Indonesia #StartupLessons #UserExperience

After 11 years working in a clinic, I decided it was time for a change. I have always loved being a vet, but there was one thing that continued to trouble me. Day after day, I would see anxious pets that were so terrified of the clinic environment that we would have to sedate them just to examine them. I knew there had to be a better way. So, in 2023, I took the leap and founded Doorstep Vet. The idea was simple: bring compassionate, high-quality veterinary care to pets in the one place they feel safest - their own home. Today, our team of 4 vets does around 30 home visits a week, and every single one is a reminder of why we do this. Calmer pets. Happier owners. Better medicine. Sometimes the bravest thing you can do is follow your heart.

Hardware is hard. Here’s our story. 🛠️ Our very first production run at Shelfwise didn’t go as planned. 400 labels shipped with a faulty battery contact. 😞 As a young hardware startup, it would have been easy to cut corners. But that’s not who we are. We made the call to recall and replace every single one of those 400 labels — at our own cost. It set us back about $7,000. Painful? Absolutely. Worth it? 100%. Because trust is everything. 🤝 We didn’t stop there. We introduced a 100% contact test at the factory. And since then? Zero contact failures across 6,000 labels. 🙌 Mistakes don’t define you. How you respond to them does. To all the hardware founders out there: own your mistakes, fix them fast, and build systems so they never happen again. 💪 #Hardware #Startups #Manufacturing #Leadership #Integrity

3 days. That's how long one spindle failure shut down our line. Years ago, I was a maintenance engineer at an auto-parts plant in Pune. One day, a spindle failed — and an entire production line ground to a halt for 3 long days. 😓 But here's the part that still haunts me: The warning signs were there. 2 weeks earlier, vibration readings had clearly shown the problem. Today, our sensors are on 410 machines across 17 plants. 🏭 Every reading is a story. Every alert is a breakdown avoided. Every plant is a step closer to the future of Indian manufacturing. 🇮🇳 Data is only powerful if someone is listening. 💡 #Manufacturing #Industry40 #PredictiveMaintenance #MakeInIndia #StartupStory
